graph.facebook.com v26.0 is a supported Meta Graph API version. Read off Meta's own SDKs, not Meta's changelog (its host is blocked by egress): facebook-python-business-sdk has targeted API_VERSION v26.0 since 2026-08-05 (facebook_business/apiconfig.py, commit 77aa28568809e8b6394b85006c45d13229a2637a, tag 26.0.0), and the facebook-business-sdk-codegen API specs were regenerated for it the same day (api_specs/specs/version.txt v25.0 -> v26.0 in c8ee473cbdfe6eab9629361568e22debd712a17d). The v26 behaviour changes reported to apply to all versions from 2026-10-27 are tracked separately in meta.v26_changes_apply_to_all_versions (#229).
facts.note: Checked 2026-09-30 against GitHub only. The v25 -> v26 spec diff (codegen 2d354f1d2ddbc27d2fd8d6dbfa69e7f8d730db87 -> 8420be6d5752c568a4f01dd608fa3cce6b2db960, which spans the v26 bump c8ee473 and the later regenerations 601cf8f4ad71d19018ca277f7d77318e77e0b072 and 8420be6) removes, among surfaces near meta-mcp: the AdsInsights fields marketing_messages_website_add_to_cart / _initiate_checkout / _purchase / _purchase_values (c8ee473); AdSet cost_bidding_mode, as field and create/update param (8420be6); AdAccountDeliveryEstimate and AdCampaignDeliveryEstimate estimate_dau and daily_outcomes_curve (c8ee473); and the CTA values GET_ACCESS, GET_UPDATES, SEE_DETAILS, SEE_MENU and VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE (c8ee473 drops them, but they had been hand-added in 670641c869f14dc411f5664878ff4a1f9e166824 three weeks earlier, so this may be a generator artifact rather than an API removal). meta-mcp names none of them. No new required create param appears on campaigns, adsets, ads or adcreatives. None of the four SDKs' CHANGELOG.md has a v26 entry (python efd8423a2e595ea8d4c04eb824ce113f2f1d68cd, nodejs 0d245ec888c1af38d68994fd7f2e24cd38abc82f, php 138fdf82d1d9f38ac250ac040f32b5f2df9bf2eb, java 0bef9f52ca443ade298f72db18e0c3c72699079d); they record SDK-only changes, not Graph behaviour. Meta's changelog was not read.

facts.claim: From 2026-10-27 three Marketing API v26.0 changes apply to every API version, so pinning an older version does not avoid them: (1) instagram_positions "explore" (the Instagram Explore Feed placement; explore_home is separate) is rejected with an error; (2) messenger_positions "story" is accepted but silently dropped, narrowing delivery without notice; (3) an ad set in the Housing, Employment or Financial Products and Services special ad categories must set targeting.targeting_automation.advantage_audience explicitly (1 or 0). meta-mcp passes targeting through unchanged and ships no guard. No shipped example names either placement or puts an ad set in a special ad category (every campaign example sends special_ad_categories: []), so (1)-(3) as reported do not break an example; most ad-set examples omit targeting_automation, which matters only if the broader readings of (3) noted below are right (#229).
facts.note: NOT confirmed by any Meta primary source reachable from here (checked 2026-09-30). Meta's generated specs cannot express any of the three: Targeting.instagram_positions and messenger_positions are list<string> with no enum, and the read-side AdCampaignPlacementGet_effective_instagram_positions / _effective_messenger_positions enums still list EXPLORE and MESSENGER_STORY at facebook-business-sdk-codegen 8420be6d5752c568a4f01dd608fa3cce6b2db960; TargetingAutomation.advantage_audience is an optional unsigned int and a conditional requirement has no spec form. No SDK CHANGELOG has a v26 entry. CORROBORATION ONLY, from third-party code on GitHub: jeffreywlai/meta-ads-mcp@fb7e1e83c528baa3f699ee69ff3ef0ae89408889 docs/v26_compatibility_audit.md (explore removed, Messenger Stories silently removed); byadsco/meta-ads-mcp@692fad75d5a875a7464f87438e1f757fd2581f87 src/meta/targeting-compat.ts (explore and messenger story removed in v26.0); mikusnuz/meta-ads-mcp@e9dfd7bfc84564492b894e146e69d897efd6130d src/tools/adsets.ts (HEC-F ad sets with relaxable targeting get ADS_TARGETING__REQUIRE_EXPLICIT_ADVANTAGE_AUDIENCE_FLAG); yvfl/faceads-mcp-v2@91592c417756de82b7454c8c4f793f65947ff84f src/tools/shared.ts (all versions from 2026-10-27, citing Meta's v26 launch post). They disagree on scope for (3): byadsco dates an explicit-flag requirement for non-default targeting to v23.0, and fl100inc/extuitive-skill@caf0724cb79451305f8f7344f86f06b31f688188 says every ad set (subcode 1870227). Read Meta's v26 changelog and the Advantage+ audience reference before 2026-10-27; if confirmed, decide whether meta_create_entity / meta_update_entity / meta_bulk_* should refuse explore and messenger story rather than let Meta error or silently narrow delivery.

facts.claim: In Graph/Marketing API v26.0 every field meta-mcp names by default exists on its node: the entity default fields (Campaign, AdSet, Ad, AdCreative, CustomAudience), the meta_list_ad_accounts defaults (AdAccount), and the insights defaults and insights-catalog metrics (AdsInsights); every catalog breakdown and action breakdown is a valid ad-account insights breakdown. In particular CustomAudience reports approximate_count_lower_bound / approximate_count_upper_bound and has no approximate_count (gone since v13.0, codegen 2c2c48483d5b33e2759aca68d7ed92dc9b1775ea). Graph rejects a request naming a field its node lacks with (#100), failing the whole read. Checked hermetically by packages/meta-mcp/tests/graph-v26-field-schema.test.ts against the fixture pinned here (#229).
facts.note: Read off Meta's generated API specs (facebook-business-sdk-codegen, the source of the four official Business SDKs), not the Graph API reference, whose host is blocked by egress; nothing was called against Meta. A spec field list is what Meta's SDKs will request, which is strong evidence but not the API's contract. On a version bump, regenerate the fixture from the codegen commit that bumps api_specs/specs/version.txt and move this value with it.

The Search Ads 360 Reporting API v0 is read-only for campaign entities — there are no campaign/ad-group/ad mutate operations, so the only governed writes are offline conversion upload/modify via the legacy v2 API.

facts.claim: Campaigns are an account-scoped sub-resource at /rest/adAccounts/{accountId}/adCampaigns for create, list, get, partial update AND delete. No account-less item path is documented, so get/update/delete cannot be built from the campaign URN alone (#210). Read from LinkedIn's Campaigns page, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: Read 2026-10-01 from the Campaigns page: get is GET /rest/adAccounts/{adAccountId}/adCampaigns/{campaignID}; the only account-less /rest/adCampaigns appears in a generic header illustration on the versioning page, which the Campaigns page contradicts.

facts.claim: Campaign groups are an account-scoped sub-resource at /rest/adAccounts/{accountId}/adCampaignGroups for create, list, get, partial update AND delete; no account-less item path is documented (#210). Read from LinkedIn's Campaign Groups page, 2026-10-01.

facts.claim: Ad targeting facets are served at GET /rest/adTargetingFacets under the versioned surface. It is a plain GET with no finder and no parameters, and returns facet descriptors (facetName, availableEntityFinders, entityTypes, adTargetingFacetUrn). linkedin_get_targeting_options now calls it that way; the q=type and q=account finders it used to send do not exist. Read from LinkedIn's Ad Targeting page, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: Read 2026-10-01: 'GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/adTargetingFacets' with no query string and no account. Not exercised against a live account.

facts.claim: GET /rest/adTargetingEntities has four finders: q=adTargetingFacet (facet; every entity of a facet), q=typeahead (facet, query, optional entityType and useCase), q=similarEntities (facet, entities=List(...)) and q=urns (urns=List(...)). locale is the record (language:en,country:US) and defaults to en/US; queryVersion is QUERY_USES_URNS. None of them documents start/count paging, so none is sent. The page is inconsistent about queryVersion: the adTargetingFacet parameter table says QUERY_USES_VALUES while every sample sends QUERY_USES_URNS; the code follows the samples. Read from LinkedIn's Ad Targeting page, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: Not exercised against a live account.

facts.claim: Targeting facets are keyed by URN urn:li:adTargetingFacet:<camelCasePluralName>. The names the code used to send are not facets: geos is locations, memberSeniorities is seniorities, companySizes is staffCountRanges, organizations is employers. ageRanges, genders, groups and interfaceLocales can only be used in the include clause. Read from LinkedIn's Targeting Criteria Facet URNs page and the Ad Targeting finder table, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: Facets in the page's table: ageRanges, audienceMatchingSegments, buyerGroups (202603+), companyCategory, degrees, dynamicSegments, employers, employersAll, employersPast, fieldsOfStudy, firstDegreeConnectionCompanies, followedCompanies, genders, groups, growthRate, industries, interests, interfaceLocales, jobFunctions, locations, memberBehaviors, profileLocations, schools, seniorities, skills, staffCountRanges, titles, titlesAll, titlesPast, yearsOfExperienceRanges. The Ad Targeting finder table also lists revenue, which the URN table omits. A create-campaign sample uses urn:li:adTargetingFacet:segments, which neither table lists; it is neither accepted specially nor refused here.

facts.claim: Targeting values use these URN namespaces: urn:li:seniority:<n> (1 Unpaid, 2 Training, 3 Entry, 4 Senior, 9 Partner, 10 Owner are shown; the pages do not label 5-8), urn:li:industry:<n>, urn:li:geo:<n>, urn:li:skill:<n>, urn:li:function:<n>, urn:li:title:<n>, urn:li:degree:<n>, urn:li:interest:<n>, urn:li:memberBehavior:<n>, urn:li:fieldOfStudy:<n>, urn:li:organization:<n> (employers and schools), urn:li:staffCountRange:(a,b), urn:li:ageRange:(a,b), urn:li:gender:MALE|FEMALE, urn:li:locale:en_US. The ad-prefixed namespaces the code used (adSeniority, adFunction, adIndustry, adCompanySize, adTitle, adInterest, adDegree, adFieldOfStudy, adSchool) do not exist. Read from LinkedIn's Targeting Criteria Facet URNs and Ad Targeting pages, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: function and title are shown only as examples on the URN page (urn:li:function:22, urn:li:title:4). The pages do not settle the seniority labels 5-8, so the targeting reference does not list them. One create-campaign sample writes employers as urn:li:company:<n>, against urn:li:organization:<n> on the URN page; the code checks neither.

facts.claim: targetingCriteria is { include: { and: [{ or: { <facet URN>: [<value URNs>] } }] }, exclude: { or: { <facet URN>: [<value URNs>] } } }: every and-clause must match, any value inside an or matches, and exclude removes members matching any of its values. locations and profileLocations cannot both be used. staffCountRanges can be included or excluded, not both. Read from LinkedIn's Campaigns, Ad Supply Forecasts, Audience Counts and Targeting Criteria Facet URNs pages, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: The same object is sent inline in a Rest.li 2.0 query on forecasts and audience counts, e.g. (include:(and:List((or:(urn%3Ali%3AadTargetingFacet%3Alocations:List(urn%3Ali%3Ageo%3A102221843)))))). The encoder reproduces LinkedIn's encoded samples byte for byte; see tests/services/linkedin-targeting-service.test.ts.

facts.claim: The locations and profileLocations facets are listed as 'typeahead only after Bing Geo Migration': they are searched with q=typeahead, not browsed with q=adTargetingFacet. Likewise schools, employers, employersPast, employersAll, groups, followedCompanies and firstDegreeConnectionCompanies have no browse finder. Read from the finder table on LinkedIn's Ad Targeting page, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: The page does not say whether the Bing geo migration has completed, or what the 'Legacy Geo' cutoff is; this follows the table as written. Not exercised against a live account.

facts.claim: Forecasts are GET /rest/adSupplyForecasts?q=criteriaV2 with required account (sponsoredAccount URN), campaignType (SPONSORED_UPDATES | SPONSORED_INMAILS | DYNAMIC), timeRange (start and end, epoch milliseconds, start in the future), targetingCriteria, and dailyBudget or totalBudget ({amount,currencyCode}). Optional: competingBid, optimizationTarget (not optimizationTargetType), campaign, creativeType, objectiveType, enableAudienceNetwork, enableAudienceExpansion, targetCost, costCap, connectedTelevisionOnly (202408+). The response is elements[{ metricType, granularity, timeSeries[{ timestamp, value, adForecastRange }] }]; it carries no audience size. Replaces the legacy POST /v2/adForecastsV2. Read from LinkedIn's Ad Supply Forecasts page, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: The page's samples write the range both as timeRange.start=... and as timeRange=(start:...,end:...); the record form is sent. Not exercised against a live account.

facts.claim: Audience counts are GET /rest/audienceCounts?q=targetingCriteriaV2&targetingCriteria=..., returning elements[{ active, total }]. total is 0 when the audience is under 300 members, to protect member privacy, and 300 is the minimum audience to run a campaign. Read from LinkedIn's Audience Counts page, 2026-10-01.
facts.note: The page's samples show no Linkedin-Version header; the client sends it on every request. Not exercised against a live account.

facts.claim: The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. No Amazon Ads rate-limit number is published in any reachable source (the vendor OpenAPI specs declare only 429). Scope is reportedly per endpoint and per LwA app (corroboration only). The 2026-05-15 live run hit 429 on the first call after 12 minutes idle, suggesting the real limit may be lower than 10/min. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

Amazon DSP entity management (campaigns = orders, ad groups = line items, ads = creatives, targets, ad associations = creative associations) is served by the Unified API as POST /adsApi/v1/{create|update|query|delete}/{campaigns|adGroups|ads|targets|adAssociations}. Every such operation requires the Amazon-Ads-AccountId and Amazon-Ads-ClientId headers and declares no Amazon-Advertising-API-Scope header; creates carry adProduct AMAZON_DSP (except adAssociations); queries take adProductFilter { include: [AMAZON_DSP] } (except adAssociations) with nextToken pagination; writes answer 207 { success[{ index, <item> }], error[{ index, errors[] }] }. The older /dsp/orders, /dsp/lineItems, /dsp/creatives, /dsp/targets and /dsp/creativeAssociations endpoints are not in the spec and not in Amazon's current Unified Postman collection (#234).
facts.note: Read 2026-09-30 off Amazon's machine-readable Unified DSP spec, amzn/ads-advanced-tools-docs @ e25aace0ec07997c113dac48f333298472243558 (2026-09-30), unified-campaign-management-migration-skills/api-specs/unified-api-dsp.json (OpenAPI 3.0.1, 'Amazon Ads API DSP Merged' 3.0), and the DSP migration guide beside it (skills/unified-dsp-cm-migration/SKILL.md). The spec is a vendor-published artifact, not the API reference on advertising.amazon.com (blocked by this repo's egress policy), and nothing here has been called against Amazon: no request on this surface has ever succeeded live. Operations used: DSPQueryCampaign/DSPCreateCampaign/DSPUpdateCampaign, DSPQueryAdGroup/DSPCreateAdGroup/DSPUpdateAdGroup, DSPQueryAd/DSPCreateAd/DSPUpdateAd, DSPQueryTarget/DSPCreateTarget/DSPDeleteTarget, and DSPQueryAdAssociation/DSPCreateAdAssociation/DSPUpdateAdAssociation/DSPDeleteAdAssociation. Conflict on the scope header: the spec declares only AccountIdHeader + ClientIdHeader and the DSP migration guide §2 says Amazon-Advertising-API-Scope is 'Not used ... Remove it', but the generic Unified Postman collection (postman/Amazon_Ads_Unified_API.postman_collection.json, same commit) sends it on every request; this server follows the spec and the DSP guide. Also unverified: that Amazon-Ads-AccountId takes the DSP advertiser ID from GET /dsp/advertisers (the value amazon_dsp_get_campaign_forecast already sends).

facts.claim: The Unified DSP spec offers no delete for campaigns, ad groups or ads (delete exists only for targets and adAssociations), its DSPUpdateState enum is ENABLED | PAUSED (ARCHIVED is read-only, 'Terminal end state'), DSP campaigns and ad groups can only be created PAUSED (DSPCreateState description), DSPQueryTargetRequest has no targetId filter, and there is no update operation for targets. So amazon_dsp_delete_entity archives orders / line items through the legacy PUT /dsp/orders|lineItems/{id} { state: ARCHIVED } call (kept from before #234, never verified), refuses creatives, and targets cannot be read by ID or updated.
facts.note: Read 2026-09-30 off Amazon's machine-readable Unified DSP spec, amzn/ads-advanced-tools-docs @ e25aace0ec07997c113dac48f333298472243558 (2026-09-30), unified-campaign-management-migration-skills/api-specs/unified-api-dsp.json (OpenAPI 3.0.1, 'Amazon Ads API DSP Merged' 3.0), and the DSP migration guide beside it (skills/unified-dsp-cm-migration/SKILL.md). The spec is a vendor-published artifact, not the API reference on advertising.amazon.com (blocked by this repo's egress policy), and nothing here has been called against Amazon: no request on this surface has ever succeeded live. The spec's only /delete/ paths are DSPDeleteAdAssociation and DSPDeleteTarget; the Unified Postman collection's delete/campaigns|adGroups|ads requests are Sponsored Products / Sponsored Brands operations (unified-api-sp.json SPDeleteCampaign etc., unified-api-sb.json), not DSP. First things a live run must establish: whether the legacy archive PUT still answers and accepts a Unified campaignId / adGroupId as its order / line item ID, and whether Amazon exposes another DSP archive path.

facts.claim: The per-process default of 5 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Corroboration only: 60 queries/min per user (raisable to 600) and 50,000/day per project. Keys are per quota user (the session's credential: a service account or one OAuth refresh-token grant), so all of a user's profiles, and reporting and trafficking calls alike, share one budget: one process sends at most the default per user, and 10 instances at most 50/min, under the corroborated 60/min per user. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Corroboration only, possibly v1-era: 2,000 requests/day per project, 4 QPS, 240/min per user. The daily cap is far tighter than any per-minute default and cannot be enforced by a per-process per-minute limiter. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0 must be sent to use Rest.li 2.0 query syntax (List(...), (k:v)); without it a call defaults to protocol 1.0, which LinkedIn plans to deprecate. Read from LinkedIn's Protocol Version page, 2026-10-01.

adAnalytics returns only impressions and clicks unless fields names metrics, and allows at most 20 fields. dateRange and pivotValues are fields and must be requested for a row to say which date and pivot value it belongs to. conversions, reach, frequency, videoStarted, clickThroughRate, costPerConversion and averageDailyReach are not fields (use externalWebsiteConversions, approximateMemberReach, videoStarts; compute rates client-side). Read from LinkedIn's Ad Analytics and schema pages, 2026-10-01.

The q=analytics pivot enum has MEMBER_COUNTRY_V2 and MEMBER_REGION_V2 as the geo pivots; MEMBER_COUNTRY and MEMBER_REGION are not in it. MEMBER_DESIGNATED_MARKET_AREA is available only from version 202609. q=statistics takes up to three pivots but none of the MEMBER_* pivots. Read from LinkedIn's schema page, 2026-10-01.

adAnalytics does not support pagination and a response is limited to 15,000 elements. It is also throttled at 45 million metric values per 5 minutes (HTTP 429). Demographic (MEMBER_*) pivots return only the top 100 values per creative per day and drop values with fewer than 3 events. Read from LinkedIn's Ad Analytics page, 2026-10-01.

LinkedIn API rate limits are daily (resetting at midnight UTC), per application and per member, vary by endpoint, and are not published in the documentation (read them from the developer portal's Analytics tab). A throttled request gets HTTP 429. The package's per-minute default is therefore a heuristic, not a mirror of LinkedIn's quota. Read from LinkedIn's Rate Limiting page, 2026-10-01.

The per-process default of 20 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Corroboration only: full-access ads_management BUC ~100,000/hour per ad account (+40 x active ads); dev tier ~300/hour (~5/min) per ad account — below this default, so dev-tier apps should lower META_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE. Keys are per Graph user (the token's `/me` id): `meta:user:{id}:account:act_{n}` for calls on a named ad account and `meta:user:{id}` for the rest, so one process sends at most the default per user per ad account plus the default per user on the account-less bucket, and 10 instances at most 10x that; two users on one ad account are two buckets, since the account id is caller input. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Primary (MicrosoftDocs/Advertising services-protocol.md): Campaign Management / Ad Insight limit calls per user per minute plus a per-customer 60-second sliding window, with NO published value; error 117 CallRateExceeded means wait 60 seconds. Keys follow both axes: every call draws on a per-user bucket and a per-customer bucket (read and write kept as separate sub-buckets of each), so one process can send up to 2x the default per user or customer across reads and writes. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Primary: every v5 operation carries an x-ratelimit-category (ads_read / ads_write / ads_analytics / org_*) and operations in one category share quota (pinterest/api-description openapi.json 5.28.0). Corroboration only for values: Standard ads_write 400/min, ads_analytics 300/min; Trial apps 300 writes/day. Keys are per Pinterest user (the token's `/v5/user_account` id): `pinterest:user:{id}:account:{adAccountId}` for the ad account's calls (entity CRUD, Pins, media, audience sizing, previews), `pinterest:user:{id}:reporting` for analytics reports and `pinterest:user:{id}` for the rest, so one process sends at most the default per user on each bucket, and 10 instances at most 10x that. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Corroboration only: Reporting API v0 3,000/min per project per user and 150,000/day per project; the legacy v2 API has daily per-project buckets with no published values. v0 and v2 share this one default, so raising it for v0 also raises unpublished v2 limits. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. No primary source (Snap publishes no Ads API spec or SDK). Corroboration only: 20 requests/second per app, 10 per token; 429 on throttle. Keys are per Snap user (`snapchat:user:{me.id}` from GET /v1/me, and `...:reporting`; a one-way hash of the credential when /v1/me gives no id), so each tenant runs two keys: one process sends at most 2x the default per user, which is at or below the token-level figure. Tokens issued to the same Snap app share the app-level figure, and the server cannot see which app issued a token, so N such tenants on one instance can send up to N times that against one app limit. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

The stats endpoint takes insight breakdowns (geo, demographic, device, interest) as the `report_dimension` query parameter, not inside `fields`: country, region, dma, country,os, gender, age, age,gender, os, os,country, make, lifestyle_category. One dimension at a time except age with gender; HOUR granularity cannot be combined with it; region/dma/make/lifestyle_category are delivery-metrics only. It replaced `dimension`/`pivots` (deprecated 2020-03-20, sunset 2020-06-20). Read first-hand from the raw page, 2026-09-30.

With DAY granularity start_time and end_time are required and must be the daily boundary for the timezone of the Ad Account, on the start of an hour; Snap's own examples end a one-day query at the next midnight (start 2020-01-25T00:00:00-08:00, end 2020-01-26T00:00:00-08:00). Read first-hand from the raw page, 2026-09-30.

Campaign create takes `objective_v2_properties` ({ objective_v2_type: AWARENESS_AND_ENGAGEMENT | APP_PROMOTION | TRAFFIC | SALES, promotion_type? }), which replaces the legacy `objective`. The legacy field is not rejected: from 2025-03-21 a translator service assigns objective_v2_properties to campaigns created with only `objective`. Ad squads require `placement_v2`; the old `placement` attribute is no longer accepted (breaking-changes log: all Ad Squads must use placement_v2, sunset 2020-06-20). Read first-hand from the raw pages, 2026-09-30.

The per-process default of 10 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Corroboration only: Basic tier 10 QPS / 600 QPM / 864,000 QPD per developer app (all tenants share it); report/task/create 60 QPM. Primary: throttle return codes in the official SDK (tiktok_code.py). Keys are per access token (`tiktok:token:{quotaClient}` and `tiktok:token:{quotaClient}:reporting`, a one-way hash of the token), so each tenant runs two keys: one process sends at most 2x the default per token. Tokens issued to the same developer app share that app's quota, and the server cannot see which app issued a token, so N such tenants on one instance can send up to N times that against one app quota. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

An async report task's output is fetched with `GET /open_api/v1.3/report/task/download/` (params: advertiser_id, task_id). For a task created with output_format CSV_DOWNLOAD or XLSX_DOWNLOAD it returns a JSON envelope with `download_url` (valid 1 hour; call again for a fresh one), `file_name` and `output_format`; for CSV_STRING it returns the CSV as a raw stream. The check endpoint returns no download URL. This is documented by TikTok (the vendor SDK spec omitted it, which is why #232 thought it undocumented). Read in a rendered browser, 2026-09-30.

`GET /open_api/v1.3/report/task/check/` returns data.status in QUEUING, PROCESSING, SUCCESS, FAILED, CANCELED (message is set when FAILED). The server previously waited for DONE, which TikTok never returns, so a real task could never look in progress or finished. Read in a rendered browser, 2026-09-30.

`POST /open_api/v1.3/report/task/create/` takes output_format (CSV_STRING default, CSV_DOWNLOAD, XLSX_DOWNLOAD) and enable_report_title_translation (default true; valid only for BASIC and AUDIENCE reports; TikTok recommends false because translated titles change). Async reports have no time-range limit, and async filters are limited to campaign_ids, adgroup_ids and ad_ids. Read in a rendered browser, 2026-09-30.

The per-process default of 60 requests/min stays within the platform's API quota across the fleet's assumed 10 instances. Primary (vendored TTD_Foundations.md:624-657): limits are per client per endpoint within a time period (usually a minute) and can be lowered dynamically; no number is published; guidance is at most 4 concurrent callers per endpoint and to honour Retry-After or wait 1 minute after a 429. Keys are per client credential (`ttd:client:{quotaClient}`, a one-way hash of the TTD-Auth token), shared by REST and GraphQL and spanning all endpoints, so each tenant's bucket is coarser than TTD's per-endpoint scoping: one process sends at most the default per client, and 10 instances at most 10x that. Recorded 2026-09-24 from a quota sweep that found no primary source (vendor doc hosts blocked); the figures below are CORROBORATION ONLY (search snippets / third-party mirrors) and the default was deliberately NOT raised on them. Re-verify on the vendor page before changing the default.

`createMutationBulk(input: { mutation, mutationVariables })`: `mutation` is ONE mutation operation, and `mutationVariables` is an array of JSON-encoded STRINGS, one per execution, each an object keyed by the mutation's variable name (`$input` -> `{ "input": { ... } }`). Read from TTD's Bulk operations page via its Monaco editor models, 2026-10-01. Not exercised against a live TTD; the declared GraphQL type of the $mutationVariables variable is not shown by the page.

TTD's bulkJob poll selects id createdAt rawResult completionPercentage completedAt status url runtimeErrors, plus `... on BulkMutationJob { mutationGqlErrors { error index } }` and `... on BulkQueryJob { queryGqlErrors }`. Per-input errors of a mutation job arrive as mutationGqlErrors with the failed input's index. The page does not list `gqlErrors`, which this server used to select from TTD's sample scripts. Read from TTD's Bulk operations page, 2026-10-01.

A bulk mutation must have fewer than 15,000 lexical tokens, include at most 1000 inputs and exactly one mutation operation; bulk operations exist only at advertiser, campaign and ad group level; mutation jobs cannot be cancelled (cancelBulkJob is for query jobs); at most 10 active and 20 queued bulk jobs; the result file expires one hour after completedAt. This server caps inputs at 100 and gates production on purpose, because the tool has never run against TTD. Read from TTD's Bulk operations page, 2026-10-01.
